title: Hybrid Stream Aggregation Benchmark for Mixed-Profile Queueing Effects
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Objective: build a reproducible harness that quantifies how continuous batching and queueing interact under mixed tenant profiles and arrival patterns, with an emphasis on tokens/sec throughput, p95 latency tracking, and automated regression detection.

Scope:
- Simulate multi-tenant request mixes (short prompts, long prompts, streaming chat, embeddings) and configurable affinity (hot prefixes) to exercise prefix/KV cache effects.
- Implement arrival models: Poisson steady-state, bursty (Erlang/ON-OFF), diurnal ramp, and priority skew with background low-priority traffic.
- Measure tokens/sec, p50/p95/p99 generation latency, queue lengths, batch sizes, batching delay distribution, and effective kernel utilization.
- End-to-end instrumentation: synthetic client generator -> load balancer config -> serving instances with runtime traces (batch ids, queue enqueue/dequeue timestamps) -> telemetry collector -> aggregator and dashboard.
- Regression detection: nightly baseline runs + bootstrap confidence intervals; alert if p95 increases >10% or tokens/sec drops >8% relative to baseline across same seed mix.

Deliverables:
1) Load generator repo (go/python) with declarative scenario files (yaml) for mixes and arrival processes.
2) Runtime instrumentation hooks to emit per-request batch metadata and queue events.
3) Data aggregator and analysis notebook that computes tokens/sec surfaces and p95 heatmaps across parameter sweeps (concurrency, arrival intensity, short/long ratio).
4) CI job that runs a small smoke sweep on merge, and a scheduled full sweep nightly with automated regression alerts.
5) Dashboard in Console showing 2D slices: intensity vs concurrency with color mapped p95 and overlayed batch-size contours.

Acceptance criteria:
- Harness can reproduce known regression case "microburst queue amplification" within ±8% of prior lab runs.
- Regression detection pipeline fires on injected slowdown experiments (simulated kernel slowdown of 15%) during nightly runs.
- Documentation and 3 example scenario YAMLs for short-chat-heavy, long-batched-heavy, and balanced multi-tenant mixes.

Risks & mitigations:
- Non-deterministic cloud noise: mitigate with repeated seeds, control-instance placement, and using dedicated test pool where possible.
- Instrumentation overhead skewing results: emit lightweight event logs and validate with a no-instrument control run.
- Large data volumes: sample events for high-throughput runs and compute summaries at ingestion time.

Notes on differences from previous harnesses:
This harness emphasizes continuous stream aggregation and its interaction with queueing delays when multiple workload classes compete for batching. Instead of only sampling arrival profiles, we add configuration knobs for prefix affinity and hot-key concentrations to exercise KV cache reuse, making the resulting surface more representative of production multi-tenant traffic mixes.
